metadata.note: Profile and Franconia Notch Railroad (NH, chartered 11 Jul 1878): a summer-only resort line from Bethlehem Junction on the Mount Washington branch to the Profile House hotel in Franconia Notch (opened 25 Jun 1879), with a branch to Bethlehem village past the Maplewood (opened 1881). 3 ft gauge to 1896, standard gauge from 1897. Each line is split into three features sharing identical geometry, one per operator (Rule 4): the P&FN itself 1879/1881-1892, the Concord and Montreal 1893-1894, and the Boston and Maine (lessee of the C&M from 29 Jun 1895) to the end. Not splits: the C&M's 1892 board control of the P&FN, the 11 Mar 1901 deed of the property to the C&M, the 1919 C&M -> B&M merger, and the 1896/97 regauging (a segment break within the B&M features). The connecting Mount Washington branch (Wing Road - Bethlehem Jct - Fabyan) is not on the map yet, so these lines connect to nothing at Bethlehem Junction.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn. Both lines end at their last passenger year (1920 Profile House line, 1925 Bethlehem Branch); track-lifting dates were not found and were not used. EXCLUDED: the Gale River logging railroad (c.1874-1877/78, logging only, whose grade the P&FN's first ~3 mi reused) - including the railway=abandoned way OSM 1094982329 running south up the Gale River, which looks like its continuation and was not drawn.
metadata.horsecar_audit: None. Steam from opening (RC1883: 3 wood-burning engines).
metadata.line_label_audit: Labels per the research report's Rule 6 notes: 'Profile and Franconia Notch: Profile House Line' / 'Bethlehem Branch', 'Concord and Montreal: ...', 'Boston and Maine: Profile House Branch' / 'Bethlehem Branch'.
not_yet_sourced: Profile House line end: 1920 (Fowler JF-NH 35) vs 1921 (ScenicNH, 1900px). Drawn to 1920. A 1921 B&M summer timetable would settle it.
Bethlehem Branch end 1925 rests on Fowler alone; no second source found.
Who ran the 1892 season - the P&FN (C&M-controlled) or the C&M itself. Drawn as P&FN (approx); the NH Railroad Commissioners' report for the year to 30 Jun 1893 would settle it.

Source conflicts recorded, not resolved: Wikipedia 'Profile House' says the railroad was built in 1872 and bought by the B&M in 1892 (uncited; contradicted by the 1878 charter, ICC opening date and the NH commissioners' returns showing the C&M, not the B&M, taking over); 1900px says the BC&M bought it (the BC&M had merged into the C&M in 1889).
Bethlehem Junction narrow-gauge transfer alignment (Pierce's Bridge, separate narrow-gauge station) vs the post-1897 junction drawn - not established (see geometry_quality).
Exact Profile House, Maplewood and Bethlehem station sites are not pinned.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates; no public timetable was read. Service was summer-only, which whole-year segments over-state.
Through B&M parlor cars Boston - Profile House in standard-gauge years: widely reported, not sourced.
references: https://nashuacitystation.org (B&M Official List of Officers, Agents and Stations 1906/1914, White Mountains Division, Profile Branch)

TRACED (~3.4 mi): Bethlehem Junction (44.2726,-71.6330, the junction node on the abandoned Mount Washington branch grade, OSM way 1103712804) south on the Profile Recreational Rail Trail / OSM railway=abandoned ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&M (note: Concord and Montreal) to 44.2447,-71.6429, ~2.3 mi; then short untagged railway=abandoned fragments in the notch - ways 1103712787 (~0.4 mi, 44.2303-44.2250), 171045427 (B&M-tagged, ~0.3 mi, 44.2087-44.2050), 171045503 (~0.2 mi), 1136622807 (~0.2 mi), 1494629762 (station end, 44.1697,-71.6853). The untagged fragments are attributed to this road by position only (no OSM operator tag, no OpenHistoricalMap way exists in the bbox). STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS (5.16 mi in all): (1) end of the rail trail 44.2447,-71.6429 to way 1103712787 at 44.2303,-71.6718, across the Gale River crossing and Gale River station area, 1.74 mi; (2) way 1103712787 south end 44.2250,-71.6745 to way 171045427 at 44.2087,-71.6850 (Lafayette Brook trestle stretch), 1.24 mi; (3) 44.2050,-71.6817 to way 171045503, 0.56 mi; (4) 171045503 to way 1136622807, 0.51 mi; (5) 1136622807 to the Echo Lake fragment (way 1287750972, its west end dropped by trim_reversals), 0.21 mi; (6) Echo Lake east shore 44.1827,-71.6864 to the Profile House end at 44.1697,-71.6854, 0.90 mi. Profile House end: hand-pinned to the south end of OSM way 1494629762 (44.1696,-71.6851), beside the Cannon Mountain Aerial Tramway base (Nominatim's tramway hit is an information board, type 'board', ~80 m away) and north of Profile Lake; the report puts the station SE of today's tramway parking lot - exact site not pinned. ERA / ALIGNMENT (Rule 2): the traced north end is the B&M-era (post-1897 standard-gauge) grade as OSM maps it. In 1879-1896 the 3 ft gauge P&FN met the standard-gauge BC&M/C&M at Bethlehem Junction by its own covered bridge over the Ammonoosuc (Pierce's Bridge) and a separate narrow-gauge station/transfer; whether the 1897 standard-gauge rebuild realigned the junction tracks to connect directly with the Mount Washington branch is NOT ESTABLISHED, so the first few hundred metres drawn for the 1879-1896 eras may follow a later junction alignment than the narrow-gauge transfer actually used. The rest of the grade is not reported as relocated. Geometry is shared identically by all three operator features (Rule 4 split).

segments.note: Profile and Franconia Notch Railroad, own trains: 3 ft gauge steam line built by the Profile House proprietors (Taft & Greenleaf) from Bethlehem Junction on the BC&M Mount Washington branch to their hotel at the head of Franconia Notch. Opened 25 Jun 1879 (ICC valuation, vol. 30). RC1883: Bethlehem Junction to Profile House 10 mi, 3 ft gauge, 3 wood-burning engines, 7 passenger cars. RC1892: P&FN's own operating return for the year to 30 Jun 1892 (the 1891 season), passenger $18,474 of $20,099 gross. 1892 passenger service is proven (Among the Clouds, 13 Jul 1892); its attribution to the P&FN rather than the Concord and Montreal is APPROXIMATE - the P&FN account ran to 30 Jun 1893 before being closed into the C&M (RC1894); the 1893 commissioners' report that would settle it was not found. Steam from opening - no animal era. Summer-season only (roughly late June to early October; RC1883 'operated only during the months of summer travel'; 1897 coupons void after 2 Oct) - the map's whole-year drawing over-states a seasonal resort line by construction. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a timetable figure: RC1892's 19,042 passenger-train-miles over ~13 mi of road imply roughly a dozen train-runs a day across both lines in a ~120-day season; ~150 min (about 3-5 trains each way a day) is arithmetic, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start 1879 from the ICC valuation (vol. 30, C&M) opening date 25 Jun 1879; operator through the 1891 season from RC1892 (P&FN's own return); 1892 service from Among the Clouds 13 Jul 1892, operator approx (as established in research/branches/profile_and_franconia_notch_railroad.txt; the tracer did not re-read these sources). headway_min is an estimate.
